output.question: Has The Washington Post announced layoffs?
output.answer: Yes. The most recent announcement I verified was an October 7, 2026 notice covering 118 workers at The Washington Post’s Springfield, Virginia, printing plant, with layoffs scheduled for December 31, 2026. The Post confirmed the notice and said it is relocating—not ending—its print operations. Earlier, on February 4, 2026, it announced company-wide layoffs affecting one-third of employees, including newsroom staff.

key_facts.fact: As reported October 15, 2026, The Washington Post notified officials on October 7 that its Springfield printing-plant relocation would result in layoffs affecting 118 workers, effective December 31, 2026.
A Washington Post spokesperson confirmed the notice was accurate and said print operations were relocating rather than ceasing.
On February 4, 2026, The Washington Post began widespread layoffs; its spokesperson said the cuts would affect one-third of all employees.

passages.quote: will result in layoffs affecting 118 workers. The layoffs are scheduled to take effect on Dec. 31.
The cuts will impact a third of all employees, according to the newspaper’s spokesperson.

caveats: The December 31, 2026 layoffs are scheduled future separations, not confirmed completed layoffs as of November 11, 2026.
The Virginia agency’s original notice could not be opened because access returned HTTP 403; the October details rely on reporting that quotes the notice and includes company confirmation.
The October notice is the most recent announcement verified in this search; it does not establish that no later announcement exists.
